parsed.explanation: The combined operative regime shows no criminalisation of trans identity, no documented border or document friction, trans-inclusive hate-crime (2018) and hate-speech (2019) law, depathologisation, and a long acceptance record (homosexuality legal since 1944). Exposure is limited: a national pool chain's changing-room ban (Oct 2025) reaches ordinary facilities but is private, contested, and of undocumented scope beyond the chain; hate-speech enforcement is weakened by a supreme-court religious-speech carve-out; minors' care has narrowed; and organised political opposition plus intimidation targets advocates (local sphere). No traveller-facing detention, custody-placement, or violence record is documented. Protections operate (national hate-crime dataset, compensation history), so documented negatives subtract only moderately.

entry_documents.exposure: No visa, entry, or document-mismatch rules for LGBTQ travellers are sourced; nearest material is a 1978 refugee-status inquiry.
entry_documents.protection: No documented entry restriction, secondary-screening practice, or marker-based denial for trans visitors.
entry_documents.interaction: Border stage unresolved; document presentation interaction with pool/facility rules not documented.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: No documented arrest, detention, or custody-placement exposure for trans visitors; hate-crime dataset records suspected offences with LGBTQI motive, implying police record rather than target.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Trans identity and expression covered by national hate-crime law since 1 July 2018; no trans-specific criminal offence.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: If a visitor were assaulted, hate-crime recording engages police; enforcement of the related hate-speech provision is contested (see remedies).

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Oct 2025: a national swimming-pool chain stopped trans customers choosing their own changing rooms — a facility-access restriction reaching ordinary public facilities; scope beyond that chain undocumented.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Legal contestation of the chain's policy is reported; no statutory changing-room ban or state facility rule documented.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Private operator restriction interacts with limited statutory facility protections; applies directly to any visitor using the chain, including accompanying a minor.

care_services.exposure: Clinical access narrowed: national institute stopped puberty blockers/hormones for under-16s (2021) and 16–18 outside trials; Feb 2022 guidance restricting blockers; gender-affirming clinics cut from seven to three (2021).
care_services.protection: Guidance, not statutory ban; 2026 data shows blocker prescriptions to trans children rose slightly; misinformation about a 'ban' circulated abroad.
care_services.interaction: Primarily resident/minor care; adult visitor emergency or continuity care not documented either way.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Organised opposition from far-right and Christian-democrat parties framed as defence of women's rights/national values; women's umbrella launched a sex-based-rights platform (2025); scholars record de-democratisation.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Official policy direction remains protective: 2024 LGR reform passed 234–94; church council voted 141 to require same-sex marriages (Nov 2025); conversion-practices bill pending.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Political framing raises probability of public confrontation but no documented state threat-framing against visitors.

minors_guardians.exposure: Travelling minor faces the same pool changing-room restriction; minor's access to gender-affirming care is narrowed (under-16 blocker/hormone stoppage, 16–18 outside trials).
minors_guardians.protection: LGR minimum age lowered to 16 with health-authority statement and guardian consent for 16–17s; conversion-practices bill pending.
minors_guardians.interaction: Care denial interaction with a visiting parent is possible but not documented for foreigners; LGR age rules are resident-facing.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Academic record of political violence and intimidation against trans advocates, feminist scholars and racialised activists, including online harassment and public vilification — aimed at the local advocacy sphere.
street_violence_police_response.protection: No documented trans-specific killings, organised targeting, or police violence against visitors; national hate-crime dataset implies investigative recording.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Traveller is not an activist actor; no documented transfer of this hostility to foreign visitors.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Hate-speech enforcement contested: imam not prosecuted (2015); preacher convicted then acquitted through the supreme court on religious-speech grounds; national dataset misses unreported hostility; pool-restriction scope beyond the chain undocumented; conversion bill enactment status unknown.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Working institutions: constitutional ruling struck forced sterilisation (2013), 2018 compensation to 600–700 people, active legal contestation of the pool policy, functioning crime-prevention reporting.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Religious-speech carve-out weakens recourse against hostile speech but not hate-crime assault recourse.

anchor_checks.comparison: Like Vessalia: equality-side law operating (trans hate-crime coverage, constitutional rulings, compensation), with isolated friction and incomplete data. Our dossier's documented pool-chain facility ban is a more concrete traveller-facing restriction than Vessalia's single rural stop, so it sits slightly below.

Meridia has trained border officers and functioning tribunals but real detention discretion. This dossier has no documented border or detention exposure at all — its worst feature is a private, contested changing-room rule — so it rates clearly above 0.75-C.

Tambera's documented care refusal required ombudsman intervention amid staff disrespect. Here no traveller-facing care refusal is documented and institutions demonstrably remediate (constitutional invalidation, compensation), so materially above 0.65-B.

parsed.synthesis: The combined regime a visitor meets is protective in law and largely accepting in practice: no trans-specific offence, no documented entry, document, detention or custody exposure, trans-inclusive hate-crime statute, depathologisation, and a decades-long acceptance record evidenced by legislative and church votes. The operative negatives are a private-pool changing-room restriction that reaches ordinary facilities (universal for users of that chain, contested, scope beyond it unknown), weakened hate-speech enforcement through a religious-speech carve-out, narrowed minors' care, and organised political opposition whose documented violence targets local advocates rather than visitors. Absence of sourced border rules leaves an open question, not an exposure. Protections are shown working, so the rating stays in the low-risk band, a step below the strongest anchors.
